_comment: Canonical tagger-only semantic-release config, injected by hyperi-ci when a repo has no .releaserc. It carries NO custom releaseRules on purpose: the version bump is semantic-release's OWN default-release-rules (commit-analyzer) -- feat->minor, fix/perf/revert->patch, breaking (! or footer)->major, everything else no release. That default IS the org SSoT; hyperi_ci.release_rules mirrors it in Python for the pre-push gate. semantic-release here analyses commits, tags HEAD, and RENDERS CHANGELOG.md; hyperi-ci's build stamps the version (hyperi-ci stamp-version) and its publish stage creates the GH release / GHCR / registry artefacts. The changelog plugin only WRITES the file -- 'hyperi-ci release-commit' puts it back on the branch afterwards, as an untagged commit, so no tag can point at machine-authored history (issue #37). Every line of the changelog preamble belongs in changelogTitle: the plugin inserts each new entry directly beneath whatever the title covers, so a paragraph left outside it ends up below the newest release. @semantic-release/exec is loaded for ONE job: generateNotesCmd prints .github/release-notes/NEXT.md, the supplement file a repo writes by hand for the release it is about to cut. semantic-release runs generateNotes on every plugin and joins the outputs, so exec must sit AFTER release-notes-generator -- the generator emits the version heading, and the supplement belongs under it, not above it. The file is optional: '|| true' turns an absent one into an empty string, and the command is plain 'cat' because generateNotes also runs in the predict-version dry-run, where hyperi-ci is not installed. 'hyperi-ci release-commit' deletes NEXT.md in the commit-back, so one supplement reaches exactly one release. No @semantic-release/git, no npm/github defaults. A repo commits its own .releaserc.json ONLY for a genuine exception (e.g. a multi-crate workspace). There is nothing project-specific to edit here.

plugins.changelogTitle:
# Changelog

Rendered by CI and committed back at the end of a release -- do not edit by
hand. Release notes also appear on the GitHub Releases page, one per tag.
